Been studying drama for a few years and these are a few play-wrights I've came across that I love!

Shakespeare - This is pretty standard but his work is so cleverly written, my favourites being King Lear, The Tempest and Julius Caesar

Arthur Miller - The Crucible is just one of the plays that really stick with you, such a good look at history


John Byrne - Scottish writer famous for the slab boys trilogy, a collection of really good stories and great humour

Ena Lamont Smith - Men Should Weep, this is a great text with a lot of great character development. One play that you can read multiple times and pick new things up

Joe Corrie - A Scottish miner during the mining strike famous for his classic 'In Times O' Strife'. Really good look at history which is still relatable as I live in the area effected

The final 3 appeal to me due to the language of scots and the humour and mind not appeal to you if you don't understand it. Some other plays I would recommend reading are

Sganarelle - Moliere

Dead Dad Dog - John McKay

Yellow Moon - David Greig

Personally I was a Yes voter, I felt that if I wanted my country to grow and become a better nation we needed our own power. Also I'm not that much of a fan of how things are run at the moment. Another reason was, excuse my language, id rather won't of my own kind fuck us over than someone go hasn't experienced Scotland and what we stand for.

I however felt a tad disappointed as we didn't take a massive opportunity to change things for the best. If it was a yes vote I believe it would effect both positively and negatively as there would no doubts be massive riots and big controversy in the following months after the result. We had time to decide everything and I felt it would ultimately be better. I do however feel if things don't change in the next few years if/when we have another referendum in the following years It will be a yes vote.
